### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s).

**17** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4b1eb0eab7ac41708a6775d1e6116ac4c038a5a3`.

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **12** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4b1eb0eab7ac41708a6775d1e6116ac4c038a5a3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `062e521fc96c9983e8ecedeea27284420c527bfe` — the merge of head `4582c20e076360cfe76027bb27a266063e2a61da` into base `4b1eb0eab7ac41708a6775d1e6116ac4c038a5a3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 062e521fc96c9983e8ecedeea27284420c527bfe && git checkout 062e521fc96c9983e8ecedeea27284420c527bfe
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4b1eb0eab7ac41708a6775d1e6116ac4c038a5a3 4582c20e076360cfe76027bb27a266063e2a61da && git checkout -B drift-repro 4b1eb0eab7ac41708a6775d1e6116ac4c038a5a3 && git merge --no-ff 4582c20e076360cfe76027bb27a266063e2a61da

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4b1eb0eab7ac41708a6775d1e6116ac4c038a5a3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4b1eb0eab7ac41708a6775d1e6116ac4c038a5a3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `4582c20e076360cfe76027bb27a266063e2a61da`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: brief 6976909080; card #35138 (body and all 10 comments, among them the claim 6975089907, the W0 decisions in amendment 6975318215, os-dev report 6976835443 and area note 6976885282); card #35144 (claim 6974958437 and every comment after it); PR #35186 (body and comments); the full diff against merge-base `7d8dcf693a` (3 files, +330/−3, 2 commits); the changeset; and the check-runs on this head. Code outside the diff was read at `origin/main` only. `origin/main` has no commit touching `packages/mcp` since the merge-base.

Face: the committed file list is `.changeset/35138-aggregate-option-order-currency.md`, `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts` and `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.aggregation-entry.test.ts`. No `packages/spec/src/**` path and no governed path is touched. `record-recognisers.mjs --paths` decides no face from the two code paths, and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` succeeded on this head. So this is the declaration face at `TIER_DEFAULT`, owed by the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line, with no ④.

### ① Derived judgments

- **CI on this head is still running.** 52 check-runs: 29 success, 16 skipped, 7 in progress, 0 failure. Still running: `Test Core` shards 1 to 7 of 10. Complete and green: `Build Core`, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, every `Type Check ·` lane, every `Lint ·` lane (among them `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, which carries the dev's NOT-MEASURED `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`), `Test Core` shards 8 to 10, `Test UI`, `Live E2E UI` and `Dogfood Regression Gate`. I judge on what is complete. The seat must see the 7 running shards finish green on this head before landing.
- **One handler, both doors: right.** `aggregate_records` is registered once, in `registerObjectTools`, which both the HTTP door and the stdio door call. Both bridges already implement `servedObjectDefinitionOf` at `origin/main` (`stdio-data-bridge.ts:1338`, `runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts:1179`), and each answers the object as that caller is served it, the same read `describe_object` projects.
- **Default group order: right.** `inDeclaredOptionOrder` reads the `groupBy` keys in order while each is a `select` or `radio` field the served definition declares options for. A date-bucketed key, a field the served definition does not show, or any other type ends the reading, and the groups under it keep the driver's order. A key's `alias` names the row column it reads. A value no option declares ranks after every declared one. `Array.prototype.sort` is stable, so groups the declared order does not tell apart keep the driver's order. The sort runs on a copy of the whole list, before the cap: `truncated` and the slice are now taken from the sorted list, and `totalGroups` is still `rows.length`, unchanged. The pins cover declared order with the null last, the alias and a second select key, the cap keeping `o00` to `o49` of 60 groups, the non-select leading key, and the field the served schema does not show. Grouping by a multi-value field is refused by the engine before any driver is asked (`group-by-structured-json-door.ts`, #20808), so no multi-value key reaches this sort.
- **`currencies`: right.** The member is present only when at least one column has a currency. `fixedAmountCurrencies` names a column only when its function is `sum`, `avg`, `min` or `max` (the set the engine's record-currency door judges) and its field, read from the served definition, has `currencyConfig.currencyMode` `fixed` with a non-empty `defaultCurrency`. `count`, `count_distinct`, a non-currency field, a `record`-mode amount and a `dynamic`-mode amount add nothing, and a field with no `currencyConfig` is `dynamic` by the spec's default. Record mode is unchanged: the engine still refuses those four functions over a `record`-mode amount unless it is grouped by that amount's code field (ADR-0144 D6, `record-currency-aggregate-door.ts` at `origin/main`). Dynamic mode is unchanged and names nothing. The fixed-currency pin and the four CONTROLs cover this.
- **Read only from the caller's served definition: right, at rule level.** Both facts come only from the definition the caller is served. A field that view does not show is neither ordered nor named, and a CONTROL pins each half. Only option values the rows already carry decide the order, and the only new text in the answer is an ISO 4217 code keyed by the caller's own alias. If the bridge has no member, finds no object, answers a non-object or throws, the tool answers exactly as before, and the CONTROL checks byte equality for both a bare and a throwing bridge. The read is skipped when the call has no group key and no amount column, and a pin counts zero reads there.
- **Tool description: right, with N1.** Three sentences are added. The record-mode sentence is true at the engine door. The select-order sentence is stated more broadly than the rule (N1).
- **Built entry of `@objectstack/mcp`: nothing removed, renamed or narrowed.** The `exports` map has only `.`. The list of `export` lines in `mcp-http-tools.ts` is identical before and after. The four new functions and the two new sets are module-private. `McpDataBridge.servedObjectDefinitionOf` changes only its jsdoc, so the `.d.ts` changes doc text only. The aggregate answer is untyped JSON text, with no output schema and no spec type (the two `aggregate_records` mentions in `packages/spec/src/data/query.zod.ts` are about the input node). Before this PR, the order of the groups in an answer to a call that sent no order was whatever the driver returned. No input that was accepted is now refused, and no member that was present is now absent.
- **SQL push-down: no finding, and the in-app sort is reasoned.** The diff adds no data query, no id materialisation and no in-app join. The default path already loaded every group and capped in the application before this PR (`totalGroups` needs the whole list). The sort reorders that same in-memory list before the existing cap, and the only new read is one metadata read per call. The PR's Acceptance notes give this reason. For the database order-and-cut path that #35144 adds, the area's answer to Q2 (A, 6976885282) pushes the declared order into the driver statement. That keeps the SQL-first rule where SQL does the cut.

Findings:

- **S1 (should-fix): the carry to #35144 is not written on #35144.** The dev's out-of-scope note names `carrier: #35144` and says "noted, not filed". Area note 6976885282 says Q2-A was "passed to area o1-C", and it lists three items for whichever of #35186 and #35144 merges main second: the explicit-order CONTROL pin, `currencies` on the order-and-cut result, and the `rows:` conflict resolved by keeping `groups` and adding `groupCount`. Card #35144 has no comment after its claim 6974958437, and #35144 has no PR yet. If #35144 merges second, its dev reads its own card, so the Q2-A rule and `currencies` on the cut path can be lost. That path would then answer select groups in driver order and amounts with no currency. To close it, post one comment on #35144 that names the Q2-A rule and the three items. No change to this head is needed. The original reviewer reads that comment as the delta.
- **N1 (nit): the tool description says the order more broadly than the rule.** "Groups of a select field come back in the order the field declares its options" reads as true for every select key. The code orders only the leading select or radio keys, and a non-select key ends the reading (the CONTROL pins this). The changeset and the jsdoc state the rule exactly. One clause in the description ("when it leads the grouping") would close it. The rows are still correct, so this has no correctness or contract effect.
- **N2 (nit): the jsdoc on `OPTION_ORDERED_GROUP_TYPES` and the PR body give the wrong reason for `multiselect`.** They say a `multiselect` "groups by a combination of options". The engine refuses every multi-value group key (#20808), so no such group reaches the tool. Prose only.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset `.changeset/35138-aggregate-option-order-currency.md`: right.** It bumps `@objectstack/mcp` at `patch`. That is the only published package the diff changes, and the test file is not published. AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist item 3 says that `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`, and that a widening outside the protocol also ships as `patch`. CI `Check Changeset` succeeded on this head.
- **`Clause-②: yes (widening)`: right.** It starts its line in both the PR body and the changeset, and the arm is one of the two allowed values. A new answer member that is present only when it has a value, and a defined order where none was promised, are widenings. Claim 6975089907 and amendment 6975318215 declared `Clause-②: yes` for PR 2 from the start.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none`: right.** No spec key, accepted value or metadata type is added. The PR reads the existing `options` and `currencyConfig` keys with their declared meaning, and `currencies` is a local answer member of an untyped tool result (ADR-0149 M1 is respected: no guidance text enters the spec).
- **Changeset prose against the diff: right.**
  - "on both the HTTP and the stdio door": one handler, two bridges (①).
  - "A value no option declares, such as a null, sorts last": the rank falls back to `rank.size`.
  - "applied to the leading select keys. From the first key that is not a select field onward, the driver's order stays": matches `inDeclaredOptionOrder` and its CONTROL.
  - "sorted before the tool's row cap": `truncated` and the slice read the sorted list.
  - "`count`, `count_distinct`, non-currency fields and `dynamic`-mode amounts carry none. A `record`-mode amount is still answered only when it is grouped by its currency code field": true (①).
  - "A field the caller's served schema does not show is never ordered by its options or named. A host whose bridge cannot serve the definition answers exactly as before": true, and pinned.
  - "Existing members (`rows`, `totalGroups`, `truncated`) are unchanged": true for their names and meaning. The order inside `rows` is the stated change.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Open question 1 (dynamic-mode amounts): answered A in 6976885282. No currency is named, the served schema does not carry the tenant's currency, and B goes to its own card only if the daily ask round shows a need. The code matches A.
- Open question 2 (after #35144, a `limit` without `orderBy` cuts in driver order): answered A in 6976885282 and owned by #35144. It is not yet written on #35144: S1.
- NOT-MEASURED gate `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (exit 3, needs every package's `dist`): answered. CI `Lint · repo & tooling gates` carries it, and it succeeded on this head.
- NOT-MEASURED explicit-order CONTROL pin: answered. `origin/main` has no ordering argument on `aggregate_records`, and `strictToolInput` refuses an `orderBy` key, so the case cannot arise on this head. The pin is owed by whichever PR merges main second: S1.
- Out-of-scope note (carrier #35144: the CONTROL pin, `currencies` on the order-and-cut result, the one-line `rows:` conflict): escalated in name, but not written where the carrier reads it: S1.
- Deviation, shared scratchpad overwritten by the PR 1 dev and all 68 gates re-run in a separate directory: process only. Only the re-run's readings are cited. Accepted.
- Deviation, overlap-check first run after the WIP pushes: process only. It was clean again before PR creation, and `origin/main` has not moved under `packages/mcp` since. Accepted.
- Deviation, commit trailers use the model-free pair: process only.
- Ablations A to D each turned the pin file red and were restored to the HEAD blob `0ed787fe69`, the blob this head carries for `mcp-http-tools.ts`. Two branches of the rule have no ablation: the date-bucket stop and the `min`/`max` members of the amount set. Each is a one-token rule that the jsdoc states. No finding.
- Docs: `content/docs/ai/natural-language-queries.mdx` and `connect-mcp.mdx` name `aggregate_records` but do not list its result members, so no page becomes untrue. No page is owed.
- Process notes: the PR is a draft. Author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay), assignee `os-warren`, so no extra author note is owed. S1 is closed by a comment on #35144, with no new head. The seat must still see the running `Test Core` shards finish green before landing (①).

### L1 review (#35138, PR 2) · 2026-11-18T11:37Z

L1: ACCEPT
Head-sha: 4582c20e076360cfe76027bb27a266063e2a61da
Read: the full diff at this head against merge base 7d8dcf693a (3 files, +330/−3), with claim 6975089907, amendment 1 6975318215 (W0 decisions and PR 2's surface), amendment 2 6976973578, os-dev report 6976835443, the final-head note 6977360328, contract record 6977026565 and its delta 6977058863.

**Fixes vs Part of.** This is PR 2 of the W0 plan, so it does not close the card. The body says `Refs #35138`, and no closing keyword appears in the body or the changeset, so a merge does not close #35138. See N1 for the form.

**Claim file surface.** Amendment 1 gives PR 2 `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts` (the `aggregate_records` handler), its tests and one changeset. The three paths are exactly that. The non-handler hunks in `mcp-http-tools.ts` are a docblock line on `McpDataBridge.servedObjectDefinitionOf` and module-private helpers the handler calls.

**Each changeset sentence against the diff.** The changeset is new, and `main` has no `.changeset/*35138*`. It bumps `@objectstack/mcp` at `patch`.
- "On both the HTTP and the stdio door": the handler lives in the shared `registerObjectTools`. Both bridges implement `servedObjectDefinitionOf` from the caller's served view: `runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts:1179` (`readObjectForCaller`) and `stdio-data-bridge.ts:1338` (`servedView.getObject`).
- "`select` or `radio` … in declared option order, an undeclared value last": `OPTION_ORDERED_GROUP_TYPES` is `select` and `radio`, and an absent value ranks `rank.size`. Both are real spec types (`field.zod.ts:77`).
- "Applied to the leading select keys; from the first non-select key the driver's order stays": the key loop `break`s on the first key that has no rank and on a date-bucketed key. The sort is stable and compares keys in order.
- "Sorted before the cap": `truncated` and the slice now read `groups`, and `totalGroups` stays `rows.length`.
- "`currencies` … alias to ISO 4217 code, present only when a column has one": `fixedAmountCurrencies` reads only `sum`, `avg`, `min` and `max` over `currencyMode: 'fixed'` with a non-empty `defaultCurrency`. The spread happens only when the map is non-empty.
- "`record`-mode is still answered only grouped by its currency code field": that is the engine's door (`record-currency-aggregate-door.ts`, ADR-0144 D6), which is unchanged here. The report re-measured it.
- "A field the served schema does not show is never ordered or named; a host that cannot serve the definition answers exactly as before": `servedFieldOf` reads only own keys of the served map, and `servedFieldsOf` returns `undefined` on a missing member, no object or a throw. Pins cover each case.
- "Existing members unchanged": `rows`, `totalGroups` and `truncated` keep their spelling and meaning.

**Tests.** There are ten new cases in `mcp-http-tools.aggregation-entry.test.ts`.
- They cover order, the alias plus second key, order before cap (60 groups, 50 kept, `o00`…`o49`), and the currencies by alias.
- CONTROL cases cover a non-select leading key, a hidden select, the count, non-currency, record-mode and dynamic-mode columns, a hidden fixed field, a bridge that lacks or throws, and a call with nothing to read (0 schema reads).
- Ablations A to D each turned the file red and were restored to the HEAD blob (report). The contract record names the two branches without an ablation: the date-bucket stop and `min`/`max`. I agree they are one-token rules, and I add no ask.

**Clause-②: yes (widening).** TIER_DEFAULT record 6977026565 is PASS on this same head, and delta 6977058863 closes S1 through 6977042103 on #35144. N1 and N2 of that record stay nits.

**Governance.** `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 35186`: NOT governed, 0 of 3 paths on the register, 333 changed lines. This is not Tier H.

**CI at this head**, from check-runs: 37 success and 16 skipped, with none failed or in progress (all ten `Test Core` shards included). The PR is mergeable `clean`.

#### Must-fix
None.

#### Should-fix
None.

#### Notes
- **N1, link form.** The L1 checklist's form for a card this PR only partly delivers is `Part of #35138`. `Refs #35138` has the same effect: it does not auto-close, and PR-body guards are green. When the last PR of the card lands, the card is closed and `pm:dispatched` is removed by hand, as for a `Part of` card.
- **N2, read only.** The two bridge comments on `servedObjectDefinitionOf` ("Rendered to nobody; the tool answers the gate's findings only") still describe `validate_expression` correctly, and `aggregate_records` renders two facts, never the definition. The interface docblock now says so. No change is asked.
- **N3, landing order.** As 6977360328 says, #35185 lands first, and whichever of #35185 and #35186 lands second merges `main` if the queue or the tree asks. A merge of `main` after this verdict comes back to L1 as a delta.
